evidence.statement: In raw genomic orientation, LC-PRIM-0004 and LC-PRIM-0005 start exactly 263 bp apart in both E. coli and yeast and share the same cross-genome coordinate diagonal.
After reverse-strand coding orientation is applied, the two blocks occupy identical coding starts in both genes: LC-PRIM-0005 at 534 and LC-PRIM-0004 at 789.
Both 1,080-bp coding regions are homologous fructose-bisphosphate aldolase genes, while whole-gene positionwise nucleotide identity is only 50.9%.
This is a validated multi-token coding grammar: separated exact primitives retain the same relative coding architecture across divergent implementations even though most nucleotide positions differ.

observations.raw_discovery_syntax: LC-PRIM-0004 -> 263 bp start-to-start -> LC-PRIM-0005 (direct genomic orientation)

semantics.validated_identity: colinear exact-fragment architecture within homologous class-II fructose-bisphosphate aldolase genes

unknowns: Whether the two exact fragments are functionally coupled or independently constrained within the same enzyme architecture.
